doc.title: Earl Watkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 7, 2002

title: Basin Street in New York opposite Mulligan and Chet Baker; drive west
summary: Scobey's band shares a bill with Mulligan and Chet Baker, then Watkins drives cross-country with George Duvivier.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: We did the Basin Street with Bob Scobey’s band in New York and we played opposite Gerry Mulligan and Chet Baker.
That’s an interesting combination of bands.

Yeah, two separate. Mulligan had his group, Chet had his group. Oh boy it was ridiculous. The band leader — I mean the manager had to take him off the stand on intermissions and bring him back after intermissions, I don’t know. He was just—
He was kind of out of it you mean? Chet?

I don’t know what his story was. And Mulligan was all business. And George Duvivier was playing with Mulligan. So what happened, oh yeah that was the first week. The second week they had Calvin Jackson, the pianist. He had written for the studios and he was a fine arranger in Hollywood and then he went back up to Canada. He is a fine pianist. And then they had the little girl that played vibes with — her name was Terry something — she played vibes with—
No. The other — Terry, the other vibraphonist.

Terry Gibbs, yeah. They did a duo at the Black Hawk. Anyhow that was the second week. But the first week okay, and then at the end of our second week there why George Duvivier, because Mulligan did the whole two weeks so George said, “Well I’m heading for the coast,” he said, “I’m driving.” He said, “Yeah,” he says he had a ’50 Cadillac with a ’54 engine in it and he loved to drive. So I said, “Well I’ll go with you. I’ll send my drums ahead and I’ll go with you.” So anyhow we drove. That was 1955. So we drove cross country, hit Vegas, and he took me to this casino. It was the daytime of course. They weren’t operating the show. But it was well known all over the country. And people from all over the country, minorities, they flocked there. And it was away from the Strip. People from here, from the Bay area, they would drive, they went down in droves, and all of them — it was that Vegas atmosphere and the shows. Lionel Hampton, Benny Carter, all the different bands that went through there. Then also Sinatra, when Basie was there naturally Sinatra was going to be there, all the stars and the movie stars and the entertainment people, they would end up there after they did their shows.
